_comment: Layer-1 outcomes — the 'fundamentals'. The ONLY things scored. A policy is judged solely by its modelled effect on these. v2 frame (2026-06-16): rebalanced so EVERY major political tradition's core goods can register as a BENEFIT, not only as a cost to others' goods — fixing the structural left-green/right-red tilt that the v1 set produced. See _history. Two TYPES of outcome: 'valenced' (scored improves/worsens) and 'directional' (a genuinely contested-valence good like border control: we report the DIRECTION of change, no good/bad verdict, and the reader supplies the value). IDs are stable identifiers; array order is display order.
classification_rule: Want it for its own sake = a fundamental (here). Valued for its effect on these = a lever (config/levers.json), scored only via effect. Test: 'Would you still want this if it had zero effect on any fundamental below?' If no, it's a lever.
_picker_groups_note: Visual grouping for the picker only — organises the 16 chips into the standard economy / public-services / society / climate buckets so it doesn't read as a flat wall. Does not affect scoring. Every outcome + directional measure must appear exactly once across the groups.
_default_selected_note: The grid opens on this balanced, poll-salient subset (cost of living, health, housing, crime, tax, work) so it isn't 15-columns-wide on load. Readers add/remove any of the full set via the picker. Deliberately spans left- and right-coded goods so the first impression isn't lopsided.
balance_rule: The set must be VALUE-BALANCED: for each major tradition (social-democratic, economic-liberal/conservative, libertarian, communitarian, green) at least one outcome must let its defining instrument score a clear 'improves'. A new right-coded outcome (tax/finances/growth) must be matched by the left's home (inequality) and vice-versa. Wording must not pre-load a contested macro premise (e.g. 'deficits are bad'). Audit badge/verdict distribution across parties as a release gate; systematic asymmetry is a methodology fault to investigate, not a finding to ship.

outcomes.name: Cost of living
outcomes.plain: Can I afford the essentials — food, energy, the bills?

outcomes.name: Affordable housing
outcomes.plain: Can I afford a decent home, to rent or buy, near my life?

outcomes.name: Healthcare
outcomes.plain: Can I get treated when I need it?

outcomes.name: Good work & fair pay
outcomes.plain: Can I earn a decent, secure living?
outcomes._distinct_from: O13 Prosperity (aggregate growth/opportunity) — O4 is the DISTRIBUTIONAL/quality side of the labour market; a policy can lift aggregate growth (O13) while wages stagnate (O4).

outcomes.name: Education & opportunity
outcomes.plain: Can my kids get a good education — and can I get the skills to get on?

outcomes.name: Security in later life
outcomes.plain: Will I have a dignified retirement and care when I'm old?

outcomes.name: Crime, justice & national security
outcomes.plain: Are my streets safe, the country secure, and does justice work?
outcomes._reframed: v2: this is now PURELY the protective good (safety, order, justice, defence). The LIBERTY COST of enforcement (surveillance, stop-and-search, detention powers) no longer nets out here — it is scored on O10. Tougher enforcement can register as an O5 'improves' and an O10 'worsens' simultaneously: two clean signals, not one muddy one.

outcomes.name: Equal treatment & democratic rights
outcomes.plain: Am I treated equally and fairly, with a fair say and due process?
outcomes._split_note: v2: old O9 'Rights & freedoms' split into O9 (equal-treatment/status — this) and O10 (negative liberty). They are RIVAL goods (anti-discrimination law advances O9 by restricting O10), so blending them made a policy score + and - on one outcome and vanish into 'mixed'. Split keeps both signals.

outcomes.name: Personal liberty & free speech
outcomes.plain: Am I free from undue state control over my speech, body, and choices?
outcomes._new: v2 (split from old O9). The home for negative liberty. Deregulation, removing mandates, or rolling back surveillance score 'improves' here; new enforcement/surveillance/coercive powers score 'worsens' here even where they 'improve' O5.

outcomes.name: Clean environment & nature
outcomes.plain: Is the air, water, and climate liveable — now and for the future?
indicators: long-term climate & sustainability for future generations
outcomes._reframed: v2: scope widened to nature/biodiversity and explicit LONG-TERM/intergenerational sustainability. dual_horizon: score near-term AND long-term (~10yr+) separately when they diverge.

outcomes.name: Tax & the money you keep
outcomes.plain: How much of what I earn do I get to keep?
outcomes._new: v2. Right-coded good's home: a tax cut can score 'improves' HERE rather than only a cost elsewhere. Its public-services counterpart is visible via O3/O7/O8 and O12, so the tradeoff shows on both sides. Party-blind, evidence-judgeable (IFS/OBR distributional analysis).

outcomes.name: Public finances & the next generation
outcomes.plain: Do the sums add up, or is the bill passed to our kids?
outcomes._new: v2. Worded MACRO-NEUTRAL on purpose: NOT 'deficits are bad'. A stimulus advocate can argue borrowing IMPROVES long-run sustainability by raising future output; a hawk argues it worsens the debt burden — BOTH on evidence (OBR/IFS). dual_horizon. This is the symmetric cost-home for unfunded spending AND unfunded tax cuts.

outcomes.name: Prosperity & living standards
outcomes.plain: Is the economy growing, with real opportunities to get on?
outcomes._new: v2. NOT raw GDP-as-telos (which would auto-penalise any environmental/long-term policy). Measures real living standards & opportunity, dual_horizon (a grid upgrade or flood defence shows near-term cost, long-term gain; a degrowth policy shows the reverse). Distinct from O4 (labour quality/distribution) and O2 (prices).

outcomes.name: Inequality & fair shares
outcomes.plain: Is the gap between the richest and the rest getting wider or narrower?
outcomes._new: v2. The LEFT's symmetric home: redistribution — the social-democratic tradition's defining instrument — had no outcome where it scored a clear 'improves' (O9 is anti-discrimination, NOT material inequality). Without this, adding O11/O12/O13 would re-tilt the board rightward. Party-blind: does the gap widen or narrow on evidence; the reader decides if they care.

outcomes.name: Community cohesion & belonging
outcomes.plain: Do people feel part of a community they can trust and belong to?
outcomes._new: v2 (panel-recommended; added on sign-off 2026-06-16). The communitarian tradition's positive home — without it, community goods only ever appear via immigration's knock-on effects. Crucially valence-UNCONTESTED: left and right both treat social trust as a good (they dispute its causes, not its desirability), so unlike immigration it fits the normal improves/worsens schema cleanly. Evidence-bearing (social-trust surveys, segregation indices, civic-participation data).

directional_measures.name: Immigration & border control
directional_measures.plain: Which way does this move immigration and border control?
directional_measures._why_directional: Whether 'more control' is an improvement is a genuine value question — scoring it improves/worsens would force the tool to take a side (any chosen direction insults half the readers), breaking party-blindness. So we report DIRECTION + magnitude + confidence, NO verdict word, and the reader supplies the valence. UI: a labelled axis (more open <-> more controlled) with the policy's position marked, captioned 'whether tighter is better is your call — we measure the move, not its merit'. CRUCIAL: every VALENCED consequence (effect on wages O4, housing O1, public finances O12, services, prosperity O13) still flows into the normal scored outcomes — only the contested 'is control itself good' question is left to the reader. Same treatment is the honest answer for sovereignty / national-identity if added later.

overlap_rule: What people feel directly is a fundamental (energy BILLS -> O2); the instrument behind it is a lever (energy POLICY -> levers). O11 (what you PAY in tax) vs O2 (prices of goods) vs O12 (the NATION's books) are distinct felt goods — a policy can move each independently; keep them separate so the tradeoff is visible. Document any new overlap here.
frame_completeness: The set must be broad enough that any policy with material life-impact maps to at least one outcome AND its intended benefit has somewhere to register as a benefit (not only its costs). If a significant policy can only ever score costs, that is a frame GAP to fix, not a verdict.
dual_horizon_rule: Outcomes flagged dual_horizon (O6, O12, O13) must assess near-term AND long-term (~10yr+) effect separately when they diverge, so a 'cost now, gain later' policy (or vice-versa) is not flattened into a single misleading verdict.
_note_rights_split: O9 (equal treatment & democratic rights) and O10 (personal liberty & free speech) were one outcome in v1. They are distinct, often rival goods and are scored independently.
_history: v1 (2026-06-11/12): 9 outcomes O1-O9, locked before first full populate. v2 (2026-06-16): REBALANCED after audits showed the v1 set encoded mainly social-democratic goods, producing a structural left-green/right-red tilt (party-blind verdicts: LibDem 187:2 improves:worsens, Reform 26:61) that threatened the tool's non-partisanship. First-principles + 5-tradition balance panel. Changes: O5 reframed to pure protective good (liberty cost moved to O10); O6 widened to nature + long-term (dual_horizon); O9 split into O9 (equal treatment) + O10 (liberty); ADDED O11 Tax, O12 Public finances (macro-neutral), O13 Prosperity (dual_horizon, not raw GDP), O14 Inequality; ADDED directional measure D1 Immigration (no good/bad verdict); ADDED O15 Community cohesion (panel-recommended, valence-uncontested) on sign-off. Set is now 15 scored (O1-O15) + 1 directional (D1). This supersedes the earlier council 'no fiscal fundamental' decision (that council answered a narrower question; the data showed the frame itself was the bias).
